ops.text: brew upgrade --cask yasyf/tap/captain-hook can brick the install when the app refuses termination: the cask's preflight runs '/Applications/Captain Hook.app/Contents/MacOS/Captain Hook --stop-and-uninstall-service', which failed with terminateRejected against a running login-item instance; the retry then removed the app before re-running that same binary (exit 127), brew's rollback also re-ran it and failed, and both Caskroom versions got purged, leaving an empty 0-byte Captain Hook.app husk in /Applications. Recovery was rmdir the husk + kill the orphaned capt-hookd serve + fresh 'brew install --cask'. The cask stanza (yasyf/homebrew-tap Casks/captain-hook.rb) should tolerate a missing binary and a terminate refusal (e.g. fall back to killall/launchctl) so upgrades survive a running app.
